Definition: shade of death, i.e. the grave (figuratively, calamity)
BiblicalUsage: Tsalmaveth is the shadow of death — the darkest valley, where death feels close enough to touch. David walked through the valley of the shadow of death and feared no evil; Isaiah says the people who walked in darkness have seen a great light; and Amos says God turns the shadow of death into morning. Job knew it as a place of dread, and the prophets knew it as a place God invades with light.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the valley of the shadow of death is real, and so is the Shepherd who walks through it with us. My position is that darkness is never the last word — God turns the shadow of death into morning. That is why David could say 'I will fear no evil': the shadow has no power where the LORD is present.
